newsitem.title: USA: Burlington Northern sells 4 rail segments.
newsitem.headline: Burlington Northern sells 4 rail segments.

text.p: Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp on Tuesday said it sold four line segments in Colorado, Nebraska and Kansas to an operating subsidiary of North American RailNet Inc, a newly formed company.
Terms of the sale to the Bedford, Texas-based company were not disclosed.

The 416 miles of railroad sold include a 225-mile segment from Sterling, Colo., to Holdrege, Neb.; a 133-mile line from Orleans Junction, Neb., to St. Francis, Kan.; a 26-mile line from Flynn, Neb., to Almena Junction, Kan.; and a 30-mile segment from Oronoque Junction to Oberlin, Kan.
Burlington Northern said Nebraska, Kansas & Colorado RailNet Inc (NKCR), a shortline railroad created by North American RailNet to serve customers on those lines, began operations on Tuesday.

Burlington Northern said it would retain pricing and routing authority. Its coal trains moving to Nebraska Public Power District's Gerald Gentleman facility will move over the shortline, operated by its crews.
